lessons.name: the quantum bridge, honest: enumerating 10 binary decisions is walking 2^10 = 1024 candidates — EXACTLY the dimension of the 10-qubit state vector the classical computation holds (n_qubit_dimension); the search space IS the basis
lessons.why: the quantum bridge, honest: enumerating 10 binary decisions is walking 2^10 = 1024 candidates — EXACTLY the dimension of the 10-qubit state vector the classical computation holds (n_qubit_dimension); the search space IS the basis

lessons.name: the optimum (3,1) is a VERTEX: both constraints are TIGHT there (x = 3 and x + y = 4) — two tight constraints in two dimensions pin a corner, the geometry of every linear optimum
lessons.why: the optimum (3,1) is a VERTEX: both constraints are TIGHT there (x = 3 and x + y = 4) — two tight constraints in two dimensions pin a corner, the geometry of every linear optimum

lessons.name: the demarcated speedup: unstructured search over 2^20 candidates takes 2^20 classical checks; Grover needs only ~sqrt = 2^10 — the EXPONENT halves (20 = 2·10) and never vanishes; a quadratic aid, not a free lunch, and this ledger's state-vector computation claims NO advantage at all

lessons.name: the 2×2 assignment instance with costs [[1,3],[2,1]]: the two matchings cost 1+1 = 2 and 3+2 = 5 — the optimum is 2, found by enumerating BOTH, the whole space checked, nothing sampled
lessons.why: the 2×2 assignment instance with costs [[1,3],[2,1]]: the two matchings cost 1+1 = 2 and 3+2 = 5 — the optimum is 2, found by enumerating BOTH, the whole space checked, nothing sampled

lessons.name: one simplex pivot strictly improves: from the vertex (3,0) worth 9 to the adjacent vertex (3,1) worth 11 — 9 < 11, the walk along an edge that ends at the optimum
lessons.why: one simplex pivot strictly improves: from the vertex (3,0) worth 9 to the adjacent vertex (3,1) worth 11 — 9 < 11, the walk along an edge that ends at the optimum

lessons.name: COMPLEMENTARY SLACKNESS on the instance: both dual prices are positive (2 > 0, 1 > 0) and both primal constraints are tight at the optimum (3+1 = 4, 3 = 3) — a positive price is paid exactly on a binding constraint, both pairs verified
lessons.why: COMPLEMENTARY SLACKNESS on the instance: both dual prices are positive (2 > 0, 1 > 0) and both primal constraints are tight at the optimum (3+1 = 4, 3 = 3) — a positive price is paid exactly on a binding constraint, both pairs verified

lessons.name: STRONG DUALITY, exact on the instance: the primal maximum 11 EQUALS the dual value 4·2+3·1 = 11 at the dual-feasible (2,1) — the gap is zero, not epsilon; the certificate and the optimum are the same number
lessons.why: STRONG DUALITY, exact on the instance: the primal maximum 11 EQUALS the dual value 4·2+3·1 = 11 at the dual-feasible (2,1) — the gap is zero, not epsilon; the certificate and the optimum are the same number

lessons.name: the primal instance max 3x+2y s.t. x+y ≤ 4, x ≤ 3: every feasible lattice point scores ≤ 11, and (3,1) scores exactly 11 — the optimum by TOTAL enumeration, exact, no epsilon
lessons.why: the primal instance max 3x+2y s.t. x+y ≤ 4, x ≤ 3: every feasible lattice point scores ≤ 11, and (3,1) scores exactly 11 — the optimum by TOTAL enumeration, exact, no epsilon

lessons.name: WEAK DUALITY on the instance: the dual point (u,v) = (2,1) is dual-feasible (u+v ≥ 3, u ≥ 2) and every feasible primal value 3x+2y stays ≤ its dual value 4u+3v = 11 — no primal point ever beats a dual bound
lessons.why: WEAK DUALITY on the instance: the dual point (u,v) = (2,1) is dual-feasible (u+v ≥ 3, u ≥ 2) and every feasible primal value 3x+2y stays ≤ its dual value 4u+3v = 11 — no primal point ever beats a dual bound
